title: RF lab card
note: Names for the simulation. This card does not replace the experiments, and it is not a guide to transmitting.

sections.title: Noise floor
sections.body: The lower trace when no desired signal is present in that slice of the display. Raising it makes a signal of the same height harder to copy.

sections.title: SNR
sections.body: Signal-to-noise ratio. In this model it is the desired level divided by the noise, interference, and desense in the passband. A ratio of about ten is about +10 dB, the same kind of power step taught with decibels earlier. Higher SNR is generally easier to copy.

sections.title: Interference
sections.body: Other energy that competes with the signal you want. It can be accidental. The lab studies the receiver's view of it.

sections.title: Narrowband interference
sections.body: A thin trace. It matters most when it enters the receiver passband.

sections.title: Broadband interference
sections.body: Energy spread across a wide part of the display. It lifts the noise floor. The desired peak can stay the same while SNR falls.

sections.title: Co-channel interference
sections.body: Energy inside the same passband as the desired signal.

sections.title: Adjacent-channel interference
sections.body: Energy just outside the passband that still spills into the receiver because the filter edge is not a brick wall.

sections.title: Receiver overload
sections.body: A very strong signal can degrade reception even when the receiver is not tuned to it. The failure is in the receiver.

sections.title: Desensitization
sections.body: Another name for that overload effect. The receiver becomes less able to recover the desired signal.

sections.title: Passband
sections.body: The shaded slice the receiver is using. Energy inside it is what this model treats as in-channel.

sections.title: Filtering
sections.body: Narrowing the passband can exclude an interferer that sits on a different frequency. It cannot recover a desired signal that is covered by energy on the same frequencies.

sections.title: Waterfall
sections.body: The same spectrum drawn again and again, newest row at the bottom, so a shape can be recognized over time. This one is simulated history.

sections.title: Jamming
sections.body: Intentional interference meant to disrupt reception. Interference can also be accidental. This lab does not transmit and does not describe how to interfere with a real system.
